predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Abstract claims 'achieving true real-time generation at 30 FPS'. However, Section 3.3 states 'After distillation, our method can achieve 8 FPS to generate the desired results', and the Appendix reports 119 ms per frame (~8.4 FPS). The claimed 30 FPS is contradicted by the paper's own measured speed and is factually incorrect.

The rotation matrix is written as R = I + sinθ · [u]_× + (1 + cosθ) · [u]_×^2. The correct Rodrigues rotation formula is R = I + sinθ · [u]_× + (1 − cosθ) · [u]_×^2. The sign of the cosθ term is wrong, making the formula mathematically incorrect.

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Table 2 reports the final model's performance on an 'indoor scenes only' subset (DINO-Score 67.8, CLIP-Score 88.2). Table 3 then uses these exact numbers to compare against Cosmos and Aether without disclosing that the evaluation is restricted to indoor scenes. The Appendix later shows a full Nymeria benchmark where PlayerOne obtains lower scores (DINO-Score 64.80, CLIP-Score 85.70 in Table 6). Presenting the higher subset results as the main comparison without clarification is misleading.
